references.text: Joseph's brothers hate him even more after he tells them his dream – paralleling their reaction in verse 8, where hatred increases because of his dreams and words.
The brothers were jealous of Joseph, while the father kept the matter in mind. This shows how the family reacted differently to his dreams of dominion.
Joseph's dreams about ruling over his brothers begin to come true when they arrive in Egypt and bow down to him with their faces to the ground.
Judah and the brothers fall down before Joseph in Egypt, a further fulfillment of the dreams for which they mocked and hated him.
Joseph's brothers fall down before him and offer to be his servants, a final fulfillment of the dream they rejected with the question, 'Will you really rule over us?'
The psalm describes how Joseph was sent ahead of his people and humbled with chains, contrasting with the exaltation the brothers refused to accept.
Stephen tells that the patriarchs were jealous of Joseph and sold him into Egypt, but God was with him – a direct parallel to the brothers' hatred and resistance toward his dreams.
A direct typological parallel where Joseph's brothers foreshadow the nations' rejection of Jesus as king.
A direct narrative connection showing the escalation from hatred toward the dreams to the plan to kill in order to prevent them.
A theological contrast where the people ask for a human king, in opposition to the brothers' rejection of God's chosen king (Joseph).
